subject: Post-demo: Decision roles, procurement path & initial security intake
messages:
From: Alicia Gomez <agomez@atlasfin.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Jacob Turner <j.turner@atlasfin.com>
Cc: 
Date: Tue, 5 May 2026 14:02:00 -0700
Subject: Thanks for the demo — next steps (stakeholders & security)

Hi Ben / Jacob,

Great demo today — appreciate the team walking us through the latency/cost examples. A couple quick asks so we can map the rest of the buying process on our end:

- Can you share a simple stakeholder map for who at Redwood we should expect to see in procurement/security calls? We want to align internal reviewers (security, legal, procurement, and the product sponsor).
- We also need a copy of any standard security questionnaire or an intake spreadsheet so our security team can start a first pass.

Decision criteria on our side (high level): reliability (SLOs), data isolation options, and demonstrable unit-costs for the expected burst pattern. I can confirm the economic owner (VP Product) and procurement contact after I loop them in.

I attached a short internal intake (for context) and recorded the demo — sharing the recording in case it helps.

Thanks,
Alicia Gomez
Director, Platform Integrations
Atlas Financial

Attachments: atlas-intake-template.pdf (pdf), demo-recording-050426.mp4 (video)

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Alicia Gomez <agomez@atlasfin.com>, Jacob Turner <j.turner@atlasfin.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 5 May 2026 16:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Thanks for the demo — next steps (stakeholders & security)

Hi Alicia — thanks for the clear summary and for sharing the intake. Quick recap from our side and proposed next steps:

1) Stakeholders youll likely see from Redwood:
   - Ben Carter, Account Exec (me) — commercial / procurement lead
   - Marissa Cole, Solutions Engineer — technical lead for security & architecture
   - Neha Kapoor, Legal & Compliance (cc in follow-ups as needed) — contract & data protections

2) Security artifacts: Ive attached our standard security questionnaire (spreadsheet) and a short checklist for systems-in-scope to this thread. That should let your security team start a first pass.

3) Procurement path: once you confirm the economic owner, I can prepare a mutual action plan and a draft commercial term sheet (no legal redlines yet). Typical timeline: 2–4 weeks from SOC2 evidence review to PO depending on procurement windows.

Next steps:
- Alicia/Jacob: confirm the procurement contact + economic buyer name (VP Product / Emily or equivalent).
- Atlas: have security fill sections 1–3 of the attached questionnaire and mark systems in/out of scope.
- Redwood: Marissa and I will schedule a 30-min kickoff with security + procurement to walk through the questionnaire and clarify boundaries.

Ill hold availability Wed/Thu morning PT — what works for you?

Best,
Ben Carter
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com | (415) 555-0134

Attachments: redwood-security-questions.xlsx (spreadsheet)

From: Jacob Turner <j.turner@atlasfin.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Alicia Gomez <agomez@atlasfin.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@atlasfin.com>
Date: Wed, 6 May 2026 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Thanks for the demo — next steps (stakeholders & security)

Thanks — quick clarifications from our side:

- Economic buyer is likely our VP Product, Emily Park (Ill introduce formally tomorrow).
- Procurement lead is procurement@atlasfin.com (CCd). They handle standard T&Cs and PO timing.
- Decision criteria: VP Product will weigh reliability (95th% latency), cost per 1k tokens under a 10k qps burst, and whether private deployment (VPC/on-prem) is in scope for regulated data.

On security scope: our platform team intends to put the inference endpoints behind a private VPC during the pilot; initial systems in scope are the inference endpoints and logs retention (we do not expect to bring data stores in scope for this first phase). Procurement/security want to see the questionnaire and any SOC2 artifacts.

Happy to jump on the call you suggested. Wed/Thu AM PT works for Emily as well but Ill confirm her availability.

-Jacob
Jacob Turner
Senior Platform Manager
Atlas Financial

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alicia Gomez <agomez@atlasfin.com>, Jacob Turner <j.turner@atlasfin.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Procurement <procurement@atlasfin.com>
Date: Fri, 7 May 2026 11:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Thanks for the demo — next steps (stakeholders & security)

Hi Alicia / Jacob — looping in Neha on legal/compliance and procurement likewise. Thanks for the clarity on decision criteria and the initial systems boundary. Ive attached the security questionnaire (same spreadsheet Ben included) with a pre-filled "what we need from you" column to speed the review. A few notes to make the intake actionable:

- Systems in scope (pilot): inference endpoints (private VPC), KV caches, request/response logs for 30 days. Data stores (customer DBs) explicitly out of scope for pilot — please flag if that expectation differs.
- Evidence we can provide quickly: SOC 2 summary, encryption-at-rest/transport writeups, KMS integration notes, and sample audit log export. If youd like a deeper dive we can include a short architecture walkthrough with our infra engineer.
- Timeline: If Atlass security team completes the questionnaire by next Tue (13 May), we can have a follow-up call the week of May 18 to review answers and identify blockers. That keeps the procurement window (PO) on track for late May/early June.

Proposed 30-min kickoff slots (PT):
- Tue 5/12 10:00–10:30
- Wed 5/13 09:00–09:30
- Thu 5/14 08:30–09:00

Please pick a slot and well send a meeting invite with an agenda (questionnaire walkthrough + evidence map).

Best,
Marissa Cole
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com | (415) 555-0199

Attachments: redwood-security-questions.xlsx (updated), evidence-index.pdf
